iCARE: Individualized Coherent Absolute Risk Estimation

Source: R/iCARE-package.R
iCARE-package.Rd

iCARE builds, applies and validates models for the absolute risk of a disease. An absolute risk model combines

  1. a model for the relative risks of the risk factors, typically estimated in a cohort or case-control study,

  2. a reference dataset of risk factors representing the population in which the model is applied,

  3. the population's age-specific disease incidence rates, and

  4. optionally, age-specific rates of competing mortality.

The main functions are

  • computeAbsoluteRisk(): estimate absolute risks for covariate and/or SNP profiles, including profiles with missing risk factors;

  • computeAbsoluteRiskSplitInterval(): the same when the relative-risk model or the risk-factor distribution changes at a cut age;

  • ModelValidation(): validate a model in a cohort or nested case-control study (calibration and discrimination);

  • plotModelValidation(): publication-ready figures of a validation.

Unofficial distribution

This is an unofficial, refactored distribution of iCARE. The official package is distributed by Bioconductor (https://bioconductor.org/packages/iCARE/) and on GitHub (https://github.com/parichoy/iCARE). This version keeps the user-facing interface, fixes known defects and has no compiled code; see vignette("differences", package = "iCARE") for every difference.

References

Pal Choudhury P, Maas P, Wilcox A, et al. (2020). iCARE: An R package to build, validate and apply absolute risk models. PLoS ONE 15(2): e0228198. doi:10.1371/journal.pone.0228198
